content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to install [product_name] hardware modules on two racks? I do not have enough space for all the modules, so I am considering installing them on two racks as is possible with other [company_name] PLCs.

Hello [user_name], The [product_name] modules must be physically connected to the controller, so installation in two separate racks is not supported. As an alternative, you would need two [product_name] units, with one set up as a slave to the other. Attached is information about configuring [product_name] in master/slave mode.

No, that's not possible. If you wish to use two racks, you need two [product_name] units. These can be connected in Master/Master or Master/Slave mode. Using Master/Master connection gives you greater flexibility.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion highlights that installing [product_name] hardware modules across two racks is not feasible due to the requirement that all modules connect directly to the controller. Unlike other [company_name] PLCs that support multi-rack setups, [product_name] is limited in this aspect. The suggested workaround involves using two devices configured in Master/Slave or Master/Master mode to address space constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking the ability to install [product_name] modules in two racks to better manage space and scale projects, similar to the flexibility offered by other PLC systems.
